hero.title: The quiz to find out who wears the pants in your relationship
hero.description: Who picks tonight's movie? Who gets the last word in an argument? Answer 20 questions on your own or together, and the quiz tells you who decides more in your relationship.
hero.subtitle: 20 questions • 4 to 8 minutes • free and no sign-up

section1.title: How does the “who wears the pants” quiz work?
section1.intro: This quiz is a game to play as a couple. It asks 20 questions about everyday decisions. For each question, you have three possible answers: “Me”, your partner's name or “Both of us equally”.
section1.p1: For example: “Who chooses where you go on vacation?” If it's almost always you, you answer “Me”. If it's your partner, you pick their name. And if you talk it over every time, you answer “Both of us equally”.
section1.p2: Not every question counts the same. For example, picking the music in the car counts less than keeping track of the money or getting the last word in an argument. At the end, the quiz adds everything up and shows each person's share on a scale.
section1.p3: Together, the first person answers the 20 questions and then hands over the phone. The second person answers without seeing what the first one chose. The quiz adds up your answers and it also tells you how many questions you agree on. That's often the funniest part, because there are couples where each one is convinced they're the one who decides!

section2.title: Where does “wear the pants” come from?
section2.p1: “To wear the pants” means to be the one in charge in a relationship. The expression goes back to a time when pants were men's clothing and the man ran the household. When people said a woman “wore the pants”, it meant she was the one who decided at home. Wiktionary still notes that it's “typically” said of a woman.
section2.p2: Americans say “pants” and the British say “wear the trousers”. There's also an older version, “wear the breeches”. The same image exists in lots of languages. The French say “porter la culotte”, the Germans “die Hosen anhaben”, the Italians “portare i pantaloni”, the Spanish “llevar los pantalones” and the Dutch “de broek aanhebben”.
section2.p3: Today the expression is mostly used as a joke, and about a man as well as a woman. The person who wears the pants is simply the one who gets the last word most often.

section3.title: Who usually decides in a couple?
section3.p1: You might think it's a matter of personality, and that's partly true. But researchers have looked into it too. In 2008, the Pew Research Center surveyed 1,260 Americans who were married or living with a partner. It asked them who made four decisions: what to do on the weekend, the household finances, big purchases for the home and what to watch on TV.
section3.p2: In 43% of couples, the woman decides in more areas than the man. In 26%, it's the man. And 31% of couples split the decisions equally. For the finances, for example, the woman manages them in 38% of couples and the man in 30%. In 28% of couples, they manage them together.
section3.p3: The survey also shows that it changes with age. People 65 and over are twice as likely as those under 30 to say they decide together. You also shouldn't confuse deciding with organizing everything. The one who picks the vacation isn't always the one who books it and packs the bags. Getting the last word and thinking of everything for two are not the same thing.

section4.title: Is it a problem if one of you decides more?
section4.p1: No, as long as it suits each of you. Some people love organizing and others are delighted when someone else picks the restaurant. Lots of couples also split things up. For example, one decides on vacations and the other on money.
section4.p2: It becomes a problem when the one who never decides no longer dares to speak up. It's also a problem when the one who decides everything is tired of carrying it all. If you often argue over who gets the last word, that's the thing to talk about.
section4.p3: There is still a limit. When one of you decides who the other is allowed to see or what they're allowed to spend, it's no longer “wearing the pants”. It's control and it's not a game anymore.

section5.title: How do you read your result?
section5.p1: The result gives each person's share of the decisions as a percentage. When you take the quiz together, it adds up your answers. For example, if you each answer “Me” to every question, the scale stays in the middle. But it also means you don't agree on anything!
section5.p2: That's why the result for two also shows the questions where you each think you're the one who decides. Then it shows the ones where you each think it's the other. They make good things to talk about over dinner.
section5.p3: This quiz is a game, just for fun, and it says nothing serious about your relationship. It's mostly a way to talk about how you make decisions, without trying to work out who's right.

seo.faqTitle: Your questions about the “who wears the pants” quiz
seo.faq1Q: How do you know who wears the pants in a relationship?
seo.faq1A: You need to look at who gets the last word on the decisions that matter, like money or vacations. That's what this quiz does, with 20 questions that count more or less. When you take it together, it also shows you whether you agree on the answer.
seo.faq2A: It means being the person who makes most of the decisions in a couple. The expression dates from a time when pants were men's clothing. The British say “wear the trousers”.
seo.faq3Q: Is it the man or the woman who decides more often?
seo.faq3A: In 2008, the Pew Research Center surveyed 1,260 people in couples in the United States. In 43% of couples, the woman decides in more areas. In 26%, it's the man. The remaining 31% split decisions equally.
seo.faq4Q: Can I take the quiz on my own?
seo.faq4A: Yes. You answer based on what happens at home and the quiz tells you who decides more in your eyes. It's still more fun together, because you each answer separately and the quiz shows you whether you agree.
seo.faq5Q: Is it a problem if the same person always decides?
seo.faq5A: Not necessarily. Some people like deciding and others would rather follow. It works very well as long as it suits each of you. But it's worth talking about if one of you feels left out of the important decisions or is tired of carrying everything.
seo.faq6Q: How can we share decisions better?
seo.faq6A: The simplest way is to split up the areas. For example, one of you gets the last word on vacations and the other on the decor. Big purchases are decided together. You can also take turns, for example for tonight's movie or for the restaurant.
